title.zh: 卷二百六十八 列傳第二十七 柴禹錫 張遜 楊守一 趙鎔 周瑩 王繼英 王顯
title.en: Volume 268 Biographies 27: Chai Yuxi, Zhang Xun, Yang Shouyi, Zhao Rong, Zhou Ying, Wang Ji Ying, Wang Xian
title.raw: 卷二百六十八 列傳第二十七 柴禹錫 張遜 楊守一 趙鎔 周瑩 王繼英 王顯 Volume 268 Biographies 27: Chai Yuxi, Zhang Xun, Yang Shouyi, Zhao Rong, Zhou Ying, Wang Ji Ying, Wang Xian

sentences.zh: 柴禹錫

translations.literal: Chai Yuxi
translations.idiomatic: Chai Yuxi

sentences.zh: 柴禹錫，字玄圭，大名人。

translations.literal: Chai Yuxi, styled Xuanguī, was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Yuxi, whose style name was Xuanguī, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 少時，有客見之曰：「子質不凡，若輔以經術，必致將相。」

translations.literal: In his youth, a guest who saw him said: "Your quality is not ordinary; if assisted with classical learning, you will surely reach general or minister."
translations.idiomatic: When he was young, a visitor who met him said, "You have uncommon talent; with the aid of classical studies, you are sure to rise to general or minister."

sentences.zh: 禹錫由是留心問學。

translations.literal: Yuxi from this devoted his mind to inquiry and learning.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Yuxi applied himself earnestly to learning.

sentences.zh: 時太宗居晉邸，以善應對，獲給事焉。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong resided at the Jin prince's establishment; because he was skilled at replying, he obtained appointment to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Taizong was still lodged at the Jin prince's residence, Yuxi won a place in his service through his skill at ready repartee.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，授供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was appointed Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo reign he was made an Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 三年，改翰林副使，遷如京使，仍掌翰林司。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was changed to Vice Hanlin Attendant, promoted to Envoy to the Capital, and still managed the Hanlin Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Vice Hanlin Attendant, then was promoted to Envoy to the Capital while continuing to head the Hanlin Office.

sentences.zh: 每夜直，上以藩府舊僚，多召訪外事。

translations.literal: Each night on duty, because he was an old associate from the prince's establishment, the emperor often summoned him to inquire about external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his night watches the emperor, remembering him as an old companion from the princely household, often called him in to ask about affairs beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 遷宣徽北院使，賜第寶積坊。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate, and a residence in Baoji Ward was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and given a mansion in Baoji Ward.

sentences.zh: 告秦王廷美陰謀，擢樞密副使。

translations.literal: He reported Prince Qin Tingmei's secret plot and was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After he denounced Prince Qin Zhao Tingmei's conspiracy, he was raised to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 踰年，轉南院使。

translations.literal: After a year, he was transferred to Southern Bureau Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was moved to Commissioner of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 服勞既久，益加勤敏。

translations.literal: Having served long, he became ever more diligent and attentive.
translations.idiomatic: The longer he served, the more diligent and alert he became.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，議廣宮城。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, the expansion of the palace city was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era the court debated enlarging the palace city.

sentences.zh: 禹錫有別業在表識中，請以易官邸，上因是薄之。

translations.literal: Yuxi had private property within the marked area and requested to exchange it for an official residence; the emperor thereby held him in lower esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi owned a private estate within the surveyed zone and asked to swap it for an official residence; the emperor took a dimmer view of him for it.

sentences.zh: 又與宰相宋琪厚善。

translations.literal: He was also on close terms with the Grand Councilor Song Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was also on intimate terms with Grand Councilor Song Qi.

sentences.zh: 會廣州徐休復密奏轉運王延範不軌狀，且言倚附大臣，無敢動搖者。

translations.literal: It happened that Xu Xiufu of Guangzhou secretly memorialized that Transport Commissioner Wang Yanfan was disloyal, and added that relying on great ministers, no one dared to move against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiufu of Guangzhou then secretly reported that Transport Commissioner Wang Yanfan was plotting treason, adding that Yanfan leaned on powerful ministers so that no one dared touch him.

sentences.zh: 上因訪琪及禹錫曰：「延範何如人？」

translations.literal: The emperor therefore asked Qi and Yuxi, saying: "What sort of man is Yanfan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon questioned Qi and Yuxi: "What manner of man is Yanfan?"

sentences.zh: 延範與琪妻為疏屬，甚言其忠勤，禹錫亦傍讚之。

translations.literal: Yanfan was a distant relation of Qi's wife; [Qi] spoke at length of his loyalty and diligence, and Yuxi also praised him from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was a distant kinsman of Qi's wife; Qi spoke at length of his loyalty and diligence, and Yuxi chimed in from the side.

sentences.zh: 上意其交通，滋不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected their collusion and was increasingly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected collusion between them and grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 禹錫又為琪請盧多遜故第，上益惡其朋比。

translations.literal: Yuxi also requested Qi's former residence of Lu Duoxun; the emperor hated their factional bonding all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi also asked on Qi's behalf for Lu Duoxun's former mansion, and the emperor detested their cliquishness all the more.

sentences.zh: 坐琪以詼諧罷相，不欲顯言之也。

translations.literal: Because Qi was removed from office for levity in speech, [the emperor] did not wish to state it explicitly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was removed from the chancellorship on grounds of flippant wit, but the emperor did not care to say so openly.

sentences.zh: 下詔切責禹錫，以驍衛大將軍出知滄州。

translations.literal: An edict sternly rebuked Yuxi; he was sent out as Valiant Guard Grand General to know Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked Yuxi and sent him out as Valiant Guard Grand General to govern Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任勤於政治，部民詣濱州列狀以聞。

translations.literal: While in office he was diligent in governance; the people of his prefecture went to Binzhou to file a collective petition to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was assiduous in administration, and the people of his district went to Bin Prefecture with a joint petition to bring it to the court's attention.

sentences.zh: 改涪州觀察使，徙澶、鎮二州駐泊部署，俄知潞州，州民乞留三載，詔獎之。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Governor of Fu Prefecture, transferred to garrison deployment of Cao and Zhen prefectures; soon he was made prefect of Lu; the people begged to keep him three years; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Governor of Fu Prefecture, then shifted to garrison command of Cao and Zhen; soon afterward he governed Lu Prefecture, where the people asked that he stay three more years and received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 徙知永興軍府，再召為宣徽北院使、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to know the Yongxing Military Commission, and again summoned as Northern Bureau Palace Commissioner and knowing Military Affairs Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Yongxing Military Commission, then summoned back as Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 至道初，制受鎮寧軍節度、知涇州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, by regulation he received command of Zhenning Army and knew Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhidao era he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenning Army and prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 入謝日，上謂曰：「由宣徽罷者不過防禦使爾，今委卿旌節，兼之重鎮，可謂優異矣。」

translations.literal: On the day he entered to give thanks, the emperor said to him: "Those dismissed from the Palace Directorate were no more than defense commissioners; now I entrust you with the command banner and also a key frontier post—this may be called exceptional favor."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he came to give thanks, the emperor told him, "Men dismissed from the Palace Directorate were lucky to keep a defense commission; now I give you a command banner and a major frontier post as well—few could call that anything but exceptional favor."

sentences.zh: 禹錫流涕哽咽而已。

translations.literal: Yuxi shed tears and could only choke with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi could only weep and choke with emotion.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，移知貝州。

translations.literal: During Xianping, he was transferred to know Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he was transferred to govern Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹兵奄至城下，禹錫內嚴備禦，寇尋引去。

translations.literal: That year Khitan troops suddenly arrived below the city wall; Yuxi strengthened defenses within; the invaders soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That year Khitan forces suddenly appeared beneath the walls; Yuxi tightened defenses within the city, and the raiders soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙陝州。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景德初，子宗慶選尚，召禹錫歸闕，令公主就第謁見，行舅姑禮，固辭不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, his son Zongqing was selected for an imperial marriage; Yuxi was summoned back to court; the emperor ordered the princess to visit the residence for the meeting and perform the in-laws' rites; he firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde his son Zongqing was chosen for an imperial marriage; Yuxi was recalled to court and ordered to receive the princess at his home for the meeting and the rites due a father-in-law from a daughter-in-law, but though he protested firmly he was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 頃之，還鎮。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十二，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-two; posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died at sixty-two and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 子宗亮，太子中允；

translations.literal: Son Zongliang, Crown Prince Middle Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongliang served as Crown Prince Middle Attendant;

sentences.zh: 宗慶，永清軍節度。

translations.literal: Zongqing, military commissioner of Yongqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing became military commissioner of Yongqing Army.

sentences.zh: 張遜，博州高唐人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun was a man of Gaotang in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun came from Gaotang in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 數歲喪父，養於叔父職方員外郎幹，後隨母歸魏仁浦家，駙馬都尉咸信，其異父弟也。

translations.literal: At several sui he lost his father and was raised by his uncle, Director of the Bureau of Armaments Qian; later he followed his mother to the household of Wei Renpu; the emperor's son-in-law Xianxin was his maternal half-brother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father when he was only a few years old and was raised by his uncle Qian, a junior officer in the Bureau of Armaments; later he followed his mother into Wei Renpu's household. The imperial son-in-law Xianxin was his half-brother on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 太宗在晉邸，召隸帳下。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the Jin establishment, he was summoned to serve under his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Taizong was lodged at the Jin prince's residence, Xun was called to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，補左班殿直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was appointed Left Guard Hall Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taiping Xingguo he was made a Left Guard Hall Retainer.

sentences.zh: 從征太原還，遷文思副使，再遷香藥庫使。

translations.literal: Returning from the campaign against Taiyuan, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Literary Bureau; again promoted to Perfume and Medicine Repository Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the Taiyuan campaign he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Literary Bureau, then again to Commissioner of the Perfume and Medicine Repository.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平後，交阯歲入貢，通關市。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Lingnan, Jiaozhi paid annual tribute and border markets were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lingnan was pacified, Jiaozhi sent tribute every year and border markets were opened.

sentences.zh: 並海商人遂浮舶販易外國物，闍婆、三佛齊、渤泥、占城諸國亦歲至朝貢，由是犀象、香藥、珍異充溢府庫。

translations.literal: Merchants along the coast then sailed to trade foreign goods; Java, Srivijaya, Parhae, Zhan City and other states also came annually to court; thus rhinoceros, elephant, incense, medicines and rare goods filled the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal merchants then sailed to trade in foreign goods, while Java, Srivijaya, Parhae, Champa, and other lands also sent annual missions to court, so that rhinoceros horn, ivory, aromatics, medicinals, and other rarities overflowed the storehouses.

sentences.zh: 遜請於京置榷易署，稍增其價，聽商入金帛市之，恣其販鬻，歲可獲錢五十萬緡，以濟經費。

translations.literal: Xun requested establishing a government monopoly market office in the capital, slightly raising prices, allowing merchants to purchase with gold and silk, permitting free resale—annually about five hundred thousand strings could be obtained to supplement expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Xun proposed setting up a state trading office in the capital, marking up prices slightly, letting merchants buy the goods with gold and silk and resell them freely—yielding about five hundred thousand strings a year to help meet expenses.

sentences.zh: 太宗允之，一歲中果得三十萬緡。

translations.literal: Taizong approved; in one year they indeed obtained three hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed, and in the first year the scheme in fact brought in three hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 自是歲有增羨，至五十萬。

translations.literal: From this each year there was surplus, reaching five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the annual take kept growing until it reached five hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，錄其勞，遷領媯州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, recording his merit, he was promoted to concurrently serve as prefect of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi his service was recognized and he was promoted to concurrent prefect of Gui.

sentences.zh: 三年，與安忠並命為東上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with An Zhong he was appointed Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he and An Zhong were jointly appointed Eastern Upper Gate Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 數月，會許仲宣罷判度支，即以遜為度支使。

translations.literal: After several months, when Xu Zhongxuan was dismissed from judging the Directorate of Expenditures, Xun was immediately made Expenditures Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later, when Xu Zhongxuan left the Directorate of Expenditures, Xun was at once made Expenditures Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was promoted to Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Duangong he was made Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，授宣徽北院使、簽署樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed Northern Bureau Palace Commissioner and signing Secretariat of Military Affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and authorized to sign Bureau of Military Affairs documents.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼樞密副使、知院事。

translations.literal: Before long, he also served as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and knowing bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also became Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting head of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 與同列寇準不協，每奏事，頗相矛盾。

translations.literal: He did not harmonize with colleague Kou Zhun; each time they memorialized, they often contradicted each other.
translations.idiomatic: He did not get on with his colleague Kou Zhun, and whenever they memorialized the throne their views often clashed.

sentences.zh: 一日，遜等晚歸私第，準與溫仲舒並轡，有狂民迎馬首拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: One day Xun and others returned late to private quarters; Zhun was side by side with Wen Zhongshu in bridles, and a mad commoner met their horses and bowed shouting "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: One evening Xun and the others were late leaving for home; Zhun was riding abreast with Wen Zhongshu when a deranged commoner met their horses, bowed, and shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 街使王賓舊與遜同事晉邸，遜又嘗舉賓，雅相厚善，因奏民迎準拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Street Commissioner Wang Bin had formerly served with Xun at the Jin establishment; Xun had also recommended Bin; they were thick friends; [Bin] therefore memorialized that the commoner met Zhun bowing "Long live."
translations.idiomatic: Street Commissioner Wang Bin had once served with Xun at the Jin prince's residence, and Xun had recommended him; they were close friends, so Bin memorialized that the commoner had greeted Zhun with a bow and a cry of "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 準自辯：「實與仲舒同行，蓋遜令賓獨奏斥臣。」

translations.literal: Zhun defended himself: "I was actually traveling with Zhongshu; surely Xun had Bin alone memorialize to expel me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhun defended himself: "I was in fact riding with Zhongshu; Xun must have had Bin lodge the accusation against me alone."

sentences.zh: 辭意俱厲，因互發其私。

translations.literal: Their words were both fierce, and they exposed each other's private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides spoke fiercely and began airing each other's private wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 太宗惡之，下詔切責，遜左降右領軍衛將軍，準亦罷職。

translations.literal: Taizong detested this; an edict sternly rebuked them; Xun was demoted to Right Royal Guard General; Zhun was also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was disgusted and issued a sharp rebuke; Xun was demoted to Right Royal Guard General and Zhun was also removed from office.

sentences.zh: 會判右金吾街仗蔡玉冒奏富人子為州大校，黜官，命遜代掌其事。

translations.literal: When judging Right Golden Crow Street Patrol Cai Yu falsely memorialized a rich man's son as a prefectural senior officer, he was dismissed from office; Xun was ordered to take over that duty in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Yu, who judged the Right Golden Crow Street Patrol, was dismissed for falsely reporting a rich man's son as a prefectural senior officer, Xun was ordered to take over his duties.

sentences.zh: 西蜀李順為亂，詔發兵水陸進討，以荊渚居其要害，命遜為右驍衛大將軍、知江陵府，賜錢二百萬，白金三千兩。

translations.literal: When Li Shun raised rebellion in Western Shu, an edict ordered troops sent by land and water to attack; because Jingzhou stood at the strategic point, Xun was appointed Right Valiant Guard Grand General and made prefect of Jiangling, and was granted two million strings of cash and three thousand taels of pure silver.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled in Western Shu, the court ordered land and sea forces to mount a campaign. Because Jingzhou occupied the strategic choke point, Xun was made Right Valiant Guard Grand General and prefect of Jiangling, with grants of two million strings of cash and three thousand taels of pure silver.

sentences.zh: 遜既至，會峽路諸漕卒數千人聚江陵，有告其謀變以應蜀寇，府中議欲盡誅之。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, several thousand transport soldiers from the Gorges route had gathered at Jiangling; someone reported they plotted mutiny to support the Shu invaders, and officials in the prefecture debated executing them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun arrived, several thousand transport soldiers from the Gorges route had gathered at Jiangling. An informant reported that they planned mutiny in support of the Shu rebels, and prefectural officials debated executing them all.

sentences.zh: 遜止捕首惡楊承進等二十一人斬於市，餘黨親加慰撫，飛奏以聞。

translations.literal: Xun only arrested the ringleader Yang Chengjin and twenty others and executed them in the marketplace; to the rest he personally added consolation and comfort, and swiftly memorialized to report.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had only the ringleaders, headed by Yang Chengjin—twenty-one men in all—seized and executed in public. He personally comforted the rest and sent an urgent memorial to report the matter.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，詔以其卒分配州郡。

translations.literal: Taizong praised this; an edict ordered these soldiers distributed among prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved, and ordered the soldiers distributed among the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 數月，遜卒，年五十六，時至道元年也。

translations.literal: Several months later, Xun died at age fifty-six, in the first year of Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Xun died at fifty-six, in Zhidao 1.

sentences.zh: 贈桂州觀察使，歸葬京師。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Guizhou and buried back in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made observation commissioner of Guizhou and buried in the capital.

sentences.zh: 遜小心謹慎，徒以攀附至貴顯，其訏謀獻替無聞焉。

translations.literal: Xun was cautious and careful; he merely through clinging rose to noble prominence; his counsel and remonstrance were not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was cautious and careful but rose to eminence only through patronage; nothing is recorded of his policy proposals or remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 子敏中，初補供奉官，遜在宣徽，表言嘗業文，願改秩，即換大理寺丞，累至比部郎中。

translations.literal: Son Minzhong was first appointed Attendant Official; while Xun was at the Palace Directorate, he memorialized that he had once studied literature and wished to change rank; he was immediately exchanged to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, accumulating to Department Head in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Minzhong was first made an Attendant Official; while Xun served at the Palace Directorate, Minzhong petitioned that he had studied letters and wished to change rank, and was at once transferred to assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review, rising in time to department director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 次子虛中，娶宗室申國公女，至供奉官、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Second son Xuzhong married the daughter of the imperial clan Duke of Shen; reached Attendant Official and Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xuzhong married a daughter of the imperial clansman Duke of Shen and rose to Attendant Official and Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 敏中子先，進士及第。

translations.literal: Minzhong's son Xian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong's son Xian passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 楊守一，字象先，其先河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Shouyi, styled Xiangxian, was by origin a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouyi, whose style name was Xiangxian, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 唐末避亂，徙家宋、鄭間。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he fled disorder and moved his family between Song and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang he fled the turmoil and moved his family between Song and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 守一稍通《周易》及《左氏春秋》，事太宗於晉邸。

translations.literal: Shouyi had some mastery of the Classic of Changes and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals, and served Taizong at the Jin prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi had some mastery of the Classic of Changes and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and served the future Taizong at the Jin prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，補右班殿直。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Right Guard Hall Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, he was made a Right Guard Hall Retainer.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，出護登州兵。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he went out to oversee the troops of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he went out to oversee the troops of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，監儀鸞司。

translations.literal: Recalled, he supervised the Ceremonial Protocol Office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he supervised the Ceremonial Protocol Office.

sentences.zh: 累遷西頭供奉官，其下多貴族子弟，頗豪縱徼幸。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Western Attendant Official; beneath him were many sons of noble families, quite arrogant and grasping for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to Western Attendant Official, he had beneath him many sons of noble families who were arrogant and grasping for favor.

sentences.zh: 始置三班院，令守一專其事，考核授任，漸有條制。

translations.literal: When the Three-Rank Bureau was first established, Shouyi was put in sole charge; examining and assigning posts, regulations gradually took form.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three-Rank Bureau was first established, Shouyi was put in sole charge; through examination and appointment, regulations gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改翰林學士。

translations.literal: After a little over a year, he was changed to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year he was made Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 守一初名守素，至是詔改之。

translations.literal: Shouyi's original name was Shousu; at this time an edict changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi had originally been named Shousu; at this time an edict changed his name.

sentences.zh: 七年，與趙鎔、柴禹錫、相里勳等告秦王廷美陰謀事，擢東上閤門使兼樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with Zhao Rong, Chai Yuxi, Xiangli Xun, and others he reported Prince Qin Tingmei's secret plot, and was promoted to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and concurrent Chief Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Zhao Rong, Chai Yuxi, Xiangli Xun, and others in reporting Prince Qin Tingmei's secret plot and was promoted to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and concurrent Chief Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，改判四方館事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was changed to judge the Four Diplomatic Hostels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made judge of the Four Diplomatic Hostels.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，詔護遷雲、朔歸附安慶兵屯於潞州。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, he was ordered to escort the relocation of troops from Yun and Shuo who had submitted and garrisoned them at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was ordered to escort the relocation of troops from Yun and Shuo who had submitted and to garrison them at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉內客省使，仍兼都承旨。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Inner Reception Commissioner, still concurrently chief receiver.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Inner Reception Commissioner while still serving concurrently as chief receiver.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，授宣徽北院使、簽署樞密院事。

translations.literal: In Duangong 1 he was granted Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and authorized to sign Bureau of Military Affairs documents.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1 he was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and authorized to sign Bureau of Military Affairs documents.

sentences.zh: 是秋，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: That autumn he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，中使護葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Marshal; a palace envoy supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Marshal, and a palace envoy supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 守一性質直勤謹，無他材術，徒以肇自王府，久事左右，適會時機，故歷職通顯，飾終之禮，率加常數焉。

translations.literal: Shouyi was by nature upright, diligent and careful; he had no other talent or art; he merely originated from the prince's establishment, long served at the side, and happened upon the right moment; therefore his offices were prominent; funeral observances were generally added beyond the regular count.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was upright, diligent, and careful, but possessed no other talent; having begun in the princely household and long served at the emperor's side, he simply happened upon the right moment, and so his offices grew conspicuous and his funeral honors were usually increased beyond the norm.

sentences.zh: 子安期歷國子博士，坐事貶卒。

translations.literal: Son Anqi served as National University academician; for an offense was demoted and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anqi served as a National University academician, was demoted for an offense, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 安期子夢得，進士及第。

translations.literal: Anqi's son Mengde passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi's son Mengde passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 趙鎔，字化鈞，滄州樂陵人。

translations.literal: Zhao Rong, styled Huajun, was a man of Leling in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rong, whose style name was Huajun, came from Leling in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以刀筆事太宗於藩邸，即位，補東頭供奉官。

translations.literal: Through clerical work he served Taizong at the princely establishment; when Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Eastern Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: Through clerical work he served the future Taizong at the princely residence, and when Taizong took the throne he was made an Eastern Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 因使吳越賜國信，及錢俶納土，遣檢校帑廩，轉內酒坊副使。

translations.literal: Because he was sent to Wuyue to bestow the state seal, and when Qian Shu submitted his territory, he was dispatched to inspect the granaries and treasuries, then transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Inner Wine Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been sent to Wuyue to bestow the state seal, and when Qian Shu submitted his territory he was dispatched to inspect the granaries and treasuries, he was then transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Inner Wine Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以告秦王廷美陰事，遷六宅使，領羅州刺史。

translations.literal: For reporting Prince Qin Tingmei's secret affairs, he was moved to Commissioner of the Six Residences and also led Luozhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For reporting Prince Qin Tingmei's secret affairs, he was made Commissioner of the Six Residences and also given Luozhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 掌翰林司，擢東上閤門使。

translations.literal: He managed the Hanlin Office and was advanced to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the Hanlin Office and was advanced to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 郭贄參知政事，鎔以同府之舊，嘗有所請托，贄不從。

translations.literal: Guo Zan served as participating in governance; Rong as a former colleague of the same office had once made a request; Zan did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zan served as Vice Grand Councilor, Zhao Rong, as a former colleague in the same office, once asked a favor, but Zan refused.

sentences.zh: 鎔摭堂吏過失以聞，贄見上，白鎔私謁，即召鎔廷辯。

translations.literal: Rong collected the clerks' faults to report; when Zan saw the emperor, he stated Rong's private solicitation; the emperor immediately summoned Rong for court debate.
translations.idiomatic: Rong gathered the clerks' faults and reported them; Zan told the emperor of Rong's private solicitation, and the emperor at once summoned Rong for a hearing at court.

sentences.zh: 詞屈，出為梓、遂州都巡檢使，改左驍衛大將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: Having no words, he was sent out as combined patrol commissioner of Zi and Sui prefectures; changed to Left Valiant Guard Grand General while retaining the prefecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to answer, he was sent out as combined patrol commissioner of Zi and Sui prefectures, made Left Valiant Guard Grand General, and retained his prefectural duties.

sentences.zh: 代還，知滄州兼兵馬部署。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was made prefect of Cangzhou and also military deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended and he returned, he was made prefect of Cangzhou and also military deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎔在郡完城塹，嚴戰具。

translations.literal: Rong in the prefecture completed walls and moats, strictly prepared war equipment.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture Rong completed the walls and moats and rigorously prepared arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗數百騎至境上，聞有備，引去。

translations.literal: The enemy once came with several hundred horsemen to the border; hearing there were preparations, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy once brought several hundred horsemen to the border, but hearing that defenses were ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷左神武大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Divine Martial Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Divine Martial Grand General.

sentences.zh: 會崔翰知州，改鎔為本州鈐轄。

translations.literal: When Cui Han became prefect, Rong was changed to military commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Han became prefect, Rong was made military commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又知廬州，因對，自陳願留，不許。

translations.literal: He was also made prefect of Luzhou; at an audience he personally stated he wished to remain, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made prefect of Luzhou; at an audience he asked to remain, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 踰年，召為樞密都承旨，同掌三班，俄拜宣徽北院使、同知樞密院事，與柴禹錫並掌機務。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned as Chief Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs and jointly managed the Three Classes; soon he was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and shared headship of the Bureau of Military Affairs, managing state affairs together with Chai Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned as Chief Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs and jointly managed the Three Classes; soon he was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and shared headship of the Bureau of Military Affairs with Chai Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣吏卒變服，散之京城察事。

translations.literal: He once sent clerks and soldiers in disguised dress, scattering them through the capital to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent clerks and soldiers in disguise, scattering them through the capital to investigate affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒乘醉與賣書人韓玉鬥毆，不勝，因誣玉言涉指斥。

translations.literal: A soldier, drunk, fought with the bookseller Han Yu and was beaten; unable to win, he falsely accused Yu of remarks involving denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier, drunk, fought with the bookseller Han Yu and lost; he then falsely accused Yu of remarks involving denunciation of the throne.

sentences.zh: 禹錫等遽以聞，玉坐抵法。

translations.literal: Yuxi and the others hurriedly reported this; Yu was convicted by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi and the others hurriedly reported the matter, and Yu was convicted under the law.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋知其冤，自後廉事不復聽。

translations.literal: Taizong soon learned of his wrongful conviction; afterward he no longer heeded undercover investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong soon learned of the injustice, and afterward no longer heeded undercover investigations.

sentences.zh: 禹錫出鎮，鎔加知院事。

translations.literal: Yuxi went out to command a garrison; Rong was additionally made acting head of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuxi went out to command a garrison, Rong was additionally made acting head of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改南院使、檢校太傅，以心疾求解。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was changed to Southern Bureau Commissioner and Provisional Grand Tutor; citing heart illness he requested release.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was made Southern Bureau Commissioner and Provisional Grand Tutor; citing heart illness he asked to be released from office.

sentences.zh: 是秋，授壽州觀察使。

translations.literal: That autumn he was granted the post of Observation Commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made observation commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年三月，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the third month of Xianping 1 he died at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xianping 1 he died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈忠正軍節度，錄其三子官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Loyal and Upright Army military commission, and his three sons were recorded for office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the Loyal and Upright Army military commission, and his three sons were recorded for office.

sentences.zh: 鎔少涉獵文史，美書翰，委質晉邸，以勤謹被眷。

translations.literal: Rong in youth had dipped into literary history, excelled at calligraphy; submitted himself at the Jin establishment and through diligence and care received favor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rong had dipped into letters and history and excelled at calligraphy; he pledged himself at the Jin prince's residence and won favor through diligence and care.

sentences.zh: 本名容，太宗改為鎔，曰：「陶鎔所以成器也。」

translations.literal: His original name was Rong; Taizong changed it to a homophone written with the metal radical and said: "Pottery smelting is how vessels are formed."
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Rong; Taizong changed the written form of his name to one signifying smelting ore and said, "It is through firing clay in a kiln that vessels are formed."

sentences.zh: 鎔性好佛，多蓄古書畫。

translations.literal: Rong by nature loved Buddhism; he stored many old books and paintings.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was devoted to Buddhism and kept many old books and paintings.

sentences.zh: 三子：忠輔，西京左藏庫副使；

translations.literal: Three sons: Zhongfu, Deputy Commissioner of Western Capital Left Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zhongfu, Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury;

sentences.zh: 忠愿，虞部員外郎；

translations.literal: Zhongyuan, Ministry of Works junior officer;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan, junior officer in the Ministry of Works;

sentences.zh: 忠厚，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Zhonghou, Inner Hall Honored Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghou, Inner Hall Honored Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周瑩，瀛州景城人。

translations.literal: Zhou Ying was a man of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ying came from Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 右領軍衛上將軍景之子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of Right Royal Guard Senior General Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Right Royal Guard Senior General Zhou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景家富財，好交結，歷事唐、漢、周。

translations.literal: Jing's family was wealthy, fond of connections; had served through Tang, Han, and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing family was wealthy and fond of cultivating connections, and had served through Tang, Later Han, and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 習水利，嘗浚汴口，導鄭州郭西水入中牟渠，修滑州河堤，累遷至是官。

translations.literal: Skilled in water conservancy; had once dredged the Bian outlet, directed water west of Zhengzhou city into the Zhongmou canal, repaired the dike on the Hua Prefecture river; repeatedly promoted to this office.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in hydraulic works, had once dredged the Bian outlet, channeled the waters west of Zhengzhou's outer wall into the Zhongmou canal, and repaired the Hua Prefecture river dike, rising through repeated promotions to this post.

sentences.zh: 太宗潛邸時，瑩得給事左右。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the hidden establishment, Ying obtained appointment to serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was still in his princely residence, Ying won a place attending him.

sentences.zh: 即位，補殿直，領武騎卒巡警泉、福州。

translations.literal: Upon enthronement, appointed Hall Retainer; led martial cavalry to patrol Quan and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the enthronement he was made a Hall Retainer and led martial cavalry to patrol Quan and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 卒才數百，捕劇賊千餘，遷供奉官。

translations.literal: With troops numbering only several hundred, captured over a thousand fierce bandits; promoted to Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few hundred men he captured more than a thousand notorious bandits and was promoted to Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 天雄軍節度孫永祐、轉運使楊緘稱薦之，又使綏、銀州按邊事，還奏稱旨，擢鞍轡庫副使。

translations.literal: Tianxiong Military Commissioner Sun Yongyou and Transport Commissioner Yang Chen recommended him; also sent to Sui and Yin prefectures to inspect border affairs; on return memorial pleased the emperor; promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Saddle and Bridle Repository.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiong Military Commissioner Sun Yongyou and Transport Commissioner Yang Chen praised him; he was also sent to inspect border affairs in Sui and Yin prefectures, and on his return his memorial pleased the emperor and he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Saddle and Bridle Repository.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，為杭、睦五州都巡檢使兼杭州都監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, made combined patrol commissioner of Hang and Mu five prefectures and concurrently Hangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he became combined patrol commissioner of the five prefectures of Hang and Mu and concurrently military commissioner of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會妖僧紹倫為變，瑩擒獲之，逮捕就戮者三百餘人，人以為酷濫。

translations.literal: When the sorcerer-monk Shaolun rebelled, Ying captured him; over three hundred persons arrested and executed; people considered it cruel and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer-monk Shaolun raised a revolt, Ying captured him; more than three hundred people were arrested and put to death, and many thought it cruel and excessive.

sentences.zh: 代還，改崇儀使、滄州都監。

translations.literal: On returning from replacement duty, changed to Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and Cangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended he was made Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and military commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 召拜西上閤門使，領鎮、定、高陽關都監，加判四方館事。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Western Upper Gate Commissioner; led military commissioner of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass; added judging Four Directions Hall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Western Upper Gate Commissioner, placed in charge of the military commissioners of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, and given additional duty judging the Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 與郝守浚護塞宋州決河，俄改三路排陣鈐轄，歷知天雄軍、真定二府，就遷引進使。

translations.literal: Together with Hao Shoujun blocked the breach at Song Prefecture on the Yellow River; soon changed to Three Routes Array Formation military commissioner; successively knew Tianxiong Army and Zhending prefectures; then promoted to Introducing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With Hao Shoujun he blocked the breach in the Yellow River at Song Prefecture; soon he was made military commissioner for array formation on the three routes, successively governed Tianxiong Army and Zhending, and was then promoted to Introducing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，代還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, returned from replacement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he returned from his tour.

sentences.zh: 會李繼隆討西夏，詔瑩詣軍前，授以機事，還拜客省使，簽書樞密院諸房公事，俄兼提點宣徽諸房、鼓司、登聞院，與劉承珪並任。

translations.literal: When Li Jilong campaigned against Western Xia, an edict ordered Ying to the front, entrusted with strategy; on return appointed Guest Reception Commissioner, signing various houses of the Military Affairs Bureau routine affairs; soon also concurrently supervising Palace Directorate various houses, drum office, Petition Court, serving together with Liu Chenggui.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jilong campaigned against Western Xia, an edict sent Ying to the front and entrusted him with strategy; on his return he was made Guest Reception Commissioner and authorized to sign routine business for the various sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon also concurrently supervised the various offices of the Palace Directorate, the drum office, and the Petition Court, sharing duty with Liu Chenggui.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，承珪分使河北告諭，加領富州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded, Chenggui was separately sent to Hebei to announce; additionally led Fuyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Chenggui was separately sent to Hebei to proclaim the news, and Ying was additionally given concurrent prefect of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 上聞其母老病，閔之，特封武功郡太夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor heard his mother was old and ill; sympathized; specially enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his mother was old and ill, the emperor took pity and specially enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Wugong commandery.

sentences.zh: 秋，拜宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: In autumn appointed Northern Palace Directorate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，宣徽著位在樞密副使上，瑩表請居下，從之。

translations.literal: Previously the Palace Directorate's formal rank was above Vice Military Commissioner; Ying memorialized requesting to be below; [the emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Palace Directorate's formal rank had stood above the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; Ying memorialized asking to rank below, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，大閱，命為隨駕部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, at the great review, he was ordered as deployment accompanying the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping, at the grand review, he was appointed deployment commissioner accompanying the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 從征河朔，又為駕前馬步都部署。

translations.literal: Following the campaign in Heshuo, he was again made Grand Deployment Commissioner of Cavalry and Infantry before the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hebei campaign he was again appointed Grand Deployment Commissioner of Cavalry and Infantry before the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷南院使、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Southern Bureau Commissioner and knowing Military Affairs Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Commissioner of the Southern Bureau and head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會蜀平，部送脅從者數十百人至闕下。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, escorts sent several hundred coerced followers to below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, escorts brought several hundred coerced followers to the capital.

sentences.zh: 西川轉運使馬亮因入奏，請赦其罪遣還。

translations.literal: Western Sichuan Transport Commissioner Ma Liang, taking advantage of entering to memorialize, requested pardoning their crimes and sending them back.
translations.idiomatic: Western Sichuan Transport Commissioner Ma Liang, on coming to court, asked that their crimes be pardoned and that they be sent home.

sentences.zh: 瑩以為當盡誅之。

translations.literal: Ying considered that they should all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying held that they ought all to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 令瑩、亮廷議，上是亮議，悉原其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ying and Liang to debate at court; the emperor favored Liang's proposal and completely pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Ying and Liang debate the matter at court, sided with Liang, and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 五年，高陽關都部署闕，蕃侯無足領之者，宰相請輟宣徽使以居其任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Gaoyang Pass deployment commission was vacant; no frontier marquis was adequate to hold it; the grand councilors requested setting aside a Palace Directorate commissioner to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the post of deployment commissioner at Gaoyang Pass fell vacant, and no frontier lord seemed fit to hold it, so the councilors asked that a Palace Directorate commissioner be reassigned to the duty.

sentences.zh: 時王繼英任北院，上以瑩練達軍事，乃拜永清軍節度，兼領其任，為三路排陣使。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jiying held the Northern Bureau; the emperor, because Ying was practiced in military affairs, appointed him military commissioner of Yongqing Army, concurrently holding the post, as Three Routes Array Formation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiying then held the Northern Bureau, but the emperor, judging Ying skilled in military affairs, made him military commissioner of Yongqing Army with concurrent command of the pass and appointed him Three Routes Array Formation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瑩隸人有錢仁度者，頗有軍功，與虎翼小校劉斌相競，為殿直閻渥所發。

translations.literal: Among Ying's subordinates was Qian Rendu, who had considerable military merit; he competed with Tiger Wing junior officer Liu Bin and was exposed by Hall Retainer Yan Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Among Ying's retainers was Qian Rendu, a man of some military merit, who quarreled with a Tiger Wing junior officer named Liu Bin; the affair was exposed by Hall Retainer Yan Wo.

sentences.zh: 以瑩故，詔勿問，止徙斌隸他軍。

translations.literal: Because of Ying, an edict ordered no inquiry; only Bin was transferred to serve under another army.
translations.idiomatic: On Ying's account an edict forbade further inquiry and merely transferred Bin to another command.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，詔步兵赴寧邊軍為援。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, an edict ordered infantry to proceed to Ningbian Army as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, an edict sent infantry to reinforce Ningbian Army.

sentences.zh: 瑩至，則寇兵已去，即日還屯所。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived, the invading troops had already departed; that same day he returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Ying arrived only after the raiders had withdrawn and returned to camp the same day.

sentences.zh: 上聞曰：「瑩何不持重少留，示以不測。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and said: "Why did Ying not hold his ground a little longer and show unpredictability?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he said, "Why did Ying not stay a little longer and keep the enemy guessing?

sentences.zh: 輕於舉措，非將帥體也。」

translations.literal: To act lightly is not the manner of a general or commander."
translations.idiomatic: Such a light-handed move is unworthy of a commander."

sentences.zh: 景德初，丁內艱，起復，代王顯為天雄軍都部署兼知軍府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, he mourned his mother, was recalled from mourning, and replaced Wang Xian as Tianxiong Army deployment commissioner while also knowing military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he was mourning his mother, was recalled from mourning, and replaced Wang Xian as deployment commissioner of Tianxiong Army while also governing the military commission.

sentences.zh: 嘗召洺州騎士千五百人赴大名，道與寇直，力戰，有死傷者，瑩猶謂其玩寇，將悉誅之。

translations.literal: He once summoned fifteen hundred cavalrymen from Luozhou to Daming; on the road they met the enemy head-on, fought fiercely, and some were killed or wounded; Ying still considered them to be treating the enemy lightly and was about to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned fifteen hundred Luozhou horsemen to Daming; on the march they met the enemy head-on, fought hard, and took casualties, yet Ying still accused them of treating the enemy lightly and was about to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 詔賜金帛，諭瑩勿治其罪。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed gold and silk and instructed Ying not to punish their crime.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted them gold and silk and told Ying not to punish them.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，為駕前東西貝冀路都部署。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured north, he was made deployment commissioner of the Eastern and Western Bei-Ji routes before the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, he served as deployment commissioner of the eastern and western Bei-Ji routes before the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 明年，改知陝州，俄徙永興軍府，又移邠州，兼環慶路都部署。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to know Shan Prefecture; soon transferred to Yongxing Military Commission; again moved to Bin Prefecture, concurrently deployment commissioner of Huanqing Route.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made prefect of Shan, soon transferred to the Yongxing Military Commission, then moved to Bin Prefecture as deployment commissioner of Huanqing Route.

sentences.zh: 時夏州內屬，詔省戍兵還營，以減饋餉之費。

translations.literal: At the time Xia Prefecture had submitted; an edict ordered reducing garrison troops returned to camp to cut supply costs.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Prefecture had then submitted to the court, and an edict ordered garrison troops reduced and returned to camp to save supply costs.

sentences.zh: 仍手詔諭瑩，瑩遽奏乞留，以張邊威。

translations.literal: Moreover a handwritten edict instructed Ying; Ying hastily memorialized begging to retain them, to display frontier prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent him a handwritten instruction, but Ying at once memorialized asking to keep the troops in order to display frontier strength.

sentences.zh: 上謂瑩庸懦不智，以曹瑋代之，徙知澶州。

translations.literal: The emperor said Ying was mediocre, cowardly and unwise; Cao Wei replaced him; he was transferred to know Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Ying mediocre, timid, and dull, replaced him with Cao Wei, and transferred him to govern Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，改天平軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was changed to military commissioner of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was made military commissioner of Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，為鎮定都部署兼知定州。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Zhen-Ding deployment commissioner while also knowing Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became deployment commissioner of Zhen and Ding while also governing Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉運使奏其曠弛，徙知澶州，境內屢有寇盜，宰相以瑩任居將帥，不能以威望鎮靖，請徙他郡。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner memorialized his laxness; he was transferred to know Cao Prefecture; within the territory bandits repeatedly appeared; the grand councilors, because Ying held a general's post, could not calm by prestige, and requested moving him to another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner reported his negligence, so he was moved to Cao Prefecture, where bandits repeatedly appeared within the borders; the councilors, noting that he held a commander's post yet could not quiet the region by prestige, asked that he be shifted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「處之閑僻，適使其自偷爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Placing him in a remote quiet place will just let him steal ease."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Put him somewhere remote and quiet and you will only let him grow slack."

sentences.zh: 遂下詔督責，令其擒捕。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to supervise and rebuke him, ordering him to capture the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued rebuking him and ordering him to capture the bandits.

sentences.zh: 時發卒修河防，而軍中所給糗糧，多腐敗不可食；

translations.literal: At the time troops were mobilized to repair river defenses, but the dry rations issued in the army were mostly rotten and inedible;
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then mobilized to repair river defenses, yet much of the dry ration issued in camp was rotten and inedible;

sentences.zh: 又役使不均，瑩不加恤，以故亡命者眾。

translations.literal: also corvée labor was unevenly assigned; Ying did not show compassion; for this reason deserters were many.
translations.idiomatic: corvée duties were unevenly assigned as well, and Ying showed no concern, so deserters became numerous.

sentences.zh: 七年，入朝，復遣還鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered court; again sent back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he came to court and was again sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 又以澶淵當契丹之衝，借其廩給之厚，復命知澶州。

translations.literal: Also because Chanyuan faced the Khitan thrust, relying on its generous grain stipends, he was again ordered to know Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chanyuan lay on the Khitan line of attack and its generous grain stipends were hard to give up, he was again appointed to govern Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九年，被疾，求還京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he fell ill and requested return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he fell ill and asked to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-six; posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初諡忠穆，後改元惠。

translations.literal: At first posthumous title Zhongmu; later changed to Yuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was first given the posthumous title Zhongmu, later changed to Yuanhui.

sentences.zh: 錄其二子供奉官普、顯為內殿崇班，二孫永昌、永吉為殿直。

translations.literal: His two sons Attendant Officials Pu and Xian were enrolled as Inner Hall Honored Attendants; two grandsons Yongchang and Yongji as Hall Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Pu and Xian, both Attendant Officials, were enrolled as Inner Hall Honored Attendants, and his grandsons Yongchang and Yongji as Hall Retainers.

sentences.zh: 瑩居樞近，無他謀略，及蒞軍旅，歷藩鎮，功業無大過人者。

translations.literal: Ying dwelt near the pivot of power, had no other stratagems; when he took charge of armies and passed through frontier commands, his achievements did not greatly surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: Ying stood close to the center of power but possessed no special stratagems, and whether in command of armies or in frontier posts his achievements never greatly surpassed those of others.

sentences.zh: 故事，大禮覃慶，外藩無賜物例。

translations.literal: By precedent, at great rites extending grace, outer commands had no precedent for bestowed goods.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when great rites extended grace throughout the realm, outer commands received no gifts.

sentences.zh: 東封歲，瑩鎮澶淵，車駕所經，故特有襲衣、金帶、器帛之賜。

translations.literal: In the year of the eastern feng, Ying commanded Chanyuan, which the imperial carriage passed; therefore he specially received gifts of court robes, gold belt, vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the eastern feng sacrifice Ying held Chanyuan, which lay on the emperor's route, and so received special gifts of court robes, a gold belt, vessels, and silks.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，瑩知定州，乃預上言：「禮成，所賜望於治所支給。」

translations.literal: At the sacrifice to Fenyin, Ying knew Ding Prefecture; he beforehand memorialized: "When the rite is complete, the gifts I hope may be disbursed at my administrative seat."
translations.idiomatic: When the Fenyin sacrifice was performed, Ying was prefect of Ding and memorialized in advance, "When the rite is complete, I hope the gifts may be paid out at my administrative seat."

sentences.zh: 人咸笑之。

translations.literal: People all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 普後為崇儀副使，顯至內殿承製。

translations.literal: Pu later became Vice Honored Ceremonial Commissioner; Xian reached Inner Hall Imperial Manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Pu later became Vice Honored Ceremonial Commissioner, and Xian rose to Inner Hall Imperial Manufacture.

sentences.zh: 王繼英

translations.literal: Wang Jiying
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiying

sentences.zh: 王繼英，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiying was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiying came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少從趙普給筆劄，普自罷河陽，為少保，從者皆去，繼英趨事逾謹。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Zhao Pu in supplying brush notes; when Pu was dismissed from Heyang and became Junior Guardian, followers all left; Jiying attended him ever more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Zhao Pu by handling his correspondence; when Pu left Heyang for the post of Junior Guardian and his followers all departed, Jiying attended him with redoubled care.

sentences.zh: 普再入相，繼英隸名中書五房院。

translations.literal: When Pu again entered the chancellorship, Jiying was enrolled in the Central Secretariat's Five Houses Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu returned to the chancellorship, Jiying was enrolled in the Central Secretariat's Five Houses Office.

sentences.zh: 時真宗在藩邸，選為導吏兼內知客事。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenzong was at the prince's establishment; he was selected as guide officer while also managing inner guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Zhenzong was still in his princely residence, Jiying was chosen as guide officer and also put in charge of inner guest affairs.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，謂曰：「汝昔事趙普，朕所備知。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned him for audience and said: "You once served Zhao Pu—I am fully aware of this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him and said, "Your service to Zhao Pu is well known to me.

sentences.zh: 今奉親賢，尤宜盡節。」

translations.literal: Now serving the dear and worthy prince, you should especially devote your utmost loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you serve the dear and worthy prince, you should devote yourself all the more faithfully."

sentences.zh: 及建儲，授左清道率府副率兼左春坊謁者——謁者本宦職，副率品秩頗崇，非趨走左右者所宜為，俾兼領之，執政之誤也。

translations.literal: When the heir was established, he was appointed Left Clear Way Rate Office Vice Commander while also Left Spring Palace Usher—the usher was originally a eunuch office; the vice commander's rank was quite exalted, not what those who run about at one's side should hold; making him concurrently lead it was an error of the administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was named, he was made Vice Commander of the Left Clear Way Rate Office while also Left Spring Palace Usher—the usher's post was originally a eunuch office, and the vice commander's rank was too lofty for a man who merely attended at one's side; having him hold both was a mistake of the administration.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，擢為引進使。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was promoted to Introducing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Jiying was promoted to Introducing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，領恩州刺史兼掌閤門使，遷左神武大將軍、樞密都承旨，改客省使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he led Enzhou prefect while also managing Gate Commissioner; promoted to Left Divine Martial Grand General, Military Affairs Chief Receiver; changed to Guest Reception Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he held En Prefecture concurrently while managing the Gate Commissioners, then became Left Divine Martial Grand General and Chief Receiver of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and finally Guest Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，繼英密請車駕北巡，上從之，即命繼英馳傳詣鎮、定、高陽關閱視行宮儲頓，宣諭將士。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, Jiying secretly requested the imperial carriage tour north; the emperor followed this; immediately ordered Jiying to ride express relay to Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass to inspect palace storage and supplies, and proclaim encouragement to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, Jiying secretly urged the emperor to tour the north; the emperor agreed and at once sent him by express relay to Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass to inspect palace stores and supplies and to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 俄充澶州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Soon he filled the post of military commissioner of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as military commissioner of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會大將傅潛逗撓得罪，令繼英即軍中召還屬吏。

translations.literal: When great general Fu Qian was guilty of delay and shirking, Jiying was ordered to summon him back from the army to the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the great general Fu Qian was condemned for delay and shirking, Jiying was ordered to summon him back from the army for punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋掌三班，拜宣徽北院使，與周瑩同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon he managed the Three Classes; appointed Northern Bureau Palace Commissioner; with Zhou Ying jointly knowing Military Affairs Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took charge of the Three Classes, was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Directorate, and shared headship of the Bureau of Military Affairs with Zhou Ying.

sentences.zh: 瑩出鎮，繼英遂冠樞宥，小心慎靖，以勤敏稱，上倚賴之。

translations.literal: When Ying went out to command a post, Jiying then topped the Military Affairs precinct; careful, cautious and tranquil; known for diligence and alertness; the emperor relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying left for a frontier command, Jiying came to head the Bureau of Military Affairs; careful, steady, and known for diligence, he won the emperor's reliance.

sentences.zh: 景德初，授樞密使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, he was appointed Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舊制，樞密院使祖母及母止封郡太夫人，有詔特加國封。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the Military Affairs Commissioner's grandmother and mother were only enfeoffed as Grand Ladies of a commandery; an edict specially added state enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation a commissioner's grandmother and mother were enfeoffed only as Grand Ladies of a commandery, but an edict specially raised them to state enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 嘗因進補軍校，白上曰：「疏外之人急於攀附者，謂臣蒙蔽不為薦引。」

translations.literal: Once when advancing supplemental military officers, he told the emperor: "Distant outsiders eager to attach themselves say I conceal and do not recommend them."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while advancing supplemental military officers, he told the emperor, "Outsiders eager to attach themselves claim that I conceal their merits and refuse to recommend them."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此輩雖有夤緣，亦須因事立功，方許擢用，不可過求僥幸，卿勿復言也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though this lot may have connections, they must also achieve merit through events before promotion is permitted; they cannot excessively seek luck; do not speak of this again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "They may have connections, but they must still earn merit in actual service before they can be promoted; they must not press their luck too far, and you need say no more of it."

sentences.zh: 從幸澶州，契丹請和，諏訪經略，繼英預焉。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Cao Prefecture, when the Khitan requested peace and strategy was consulted, Jiying participated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Cao Prefecture and the Khitan sought peace, Jiying took part in the strategic consultations.

sentences.zh: 明年郊祀，加特進、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: The next year at suburban sacrifice, specially advanced to Exceptional Promotion and Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice the following year he was given Exceptional Promotion and Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 上臨哭之，賜白金五千兩，贈太尉、侍中，諡恭懿。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to mourn him; bestowed five thousand taels of white gold; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant; posthumous title Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him, granted five thousand taels of white gold, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant with the title Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 且為葬其祖父，贈其妻賈長樂郡太夫人，錄其子婿、門下親吏數十人。

translations.literal: Moreover he had his grandfather buried, enfeoffed his wife Jia as Grand Lady of Changle commandery, and enrolled several tens of his sons-in-law and personal clerks at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Jiying's grandfather buried, enfeoffed his wife Lady Jia as Grand Lady of Changle commandery, and enrolled several dozen of his sons-in-law and personal clerks.

sentences.zh: 初，繼英幼孤，寄育外氏。

translations.literal: At first Jiying was orphaned young and was fostered by his maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying had been orphaned young and was raised in his maternal clan's household.

sentences.zh: 既貴，外王父、諸舅有族殯者，時方奏遣其子營葬，會卒，特詔有司給辦焉。

translations.literal: Once honored, his maternal grandfather and various maternal uncles had clan burials pending; at the time a memorial was being submitted to send his son to arrange burial; he happened to die; a special edict ordered the relevant offices to provide for it.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose high, his maternal grandfather and uncles still had clan burials pending, and a memorial was on the point of sending his son to arrange them when Jiying died; a special edict ordered the relevant offices to handle the burials.

sentences.zh: 子遵式、遵誨、遵度、遵範，皆至顯宦。

translations.literal: Sons Zunshi, Zunhui, Zundu, and Zunfan all reached prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zunshi, Zunhui, Zundu, and Zunfan all rose to prominent office.

sentences.zh: 王顯，字德明，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, styled Deming, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, whose style name was Deming, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初為殿前司小吏，太宗居藩，嘗給事左右。

translations.literal: At first he was a minor clerk in the Hall Front Office; when Taizong resided as prince, he once attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a minor clerk in the Hall Front Office and had once attended Taizong when he was still a prince.

sentences.zh: 性謹介，不好狎，未嘗踐市肆。

translations.literal: By nature careful and upright, he did not like familiarity; he never set foot in marketplaces.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was careful and reserved, disliked familiarity, and never set foot in a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 即位，補殿直，稍遷供奉官。

translations.literal: Upon enthronement, appointed Hall Retainer; gradually promoted to Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: After the enthronement he was made a Hall Retainer and gradually promoted to Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，授軍器庫副使，遷尚食使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Armory Repository; promoted to Food Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he became Deputy Commissioner of the Armory Repository and then Food Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 踰年，與郭昭敏並為東上閤門使。

translations.literal: After a year, together with Guo Zhaomin he was appointed Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he and Guo Zhaomin were jointly appointed Eastern Upper Gate Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 八年春，拜宣徽南院使兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: In spring of the eighth year, appointed Southern Bureau Palace Commissioner while also Vice Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he was made Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是夏，制授樞密使。

translations.literal: That summer, by regulation he was appointed Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he was formally appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「卿世家本儒，少遭亂失學，今典朕機務，無暇博覽群書，能熟《軍戒》三篇，亦可免於面牆矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Your family by origin were Confucians; in youth you suffered disorder and lost learning; now you manage my secret affairs and have no leisure to broadly read all books—if you can master the three chapters of Military Admonitions, you may also escape facing a wall."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "Your family were scholars by origin, but you lost your schooling in the turmoil of youth; now you manage my secret affairs and have no time to read widely, yet if you can master the three chapters of Military Admonitions you need not stand like a man facing a blank wall."

sentences.zh: 因取是書及道德坊宅一區賜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took that book and one ward residence in Daode Ward and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him that book and a residence in Daode Ward.

sentences.zh: 其後居位既久，機務益繁，副使趙昌言、寇準鋒氣皆銳，慢顯，顯或失誤，護短終不肯改，上每面戒之。

translations.literal: Afterward, having held office long, secret affairs grew ever more numerous; Vice Commissioners Zhao Changyan and Kou Zhun were both sharp in edge; they slighted Xian; Xian sometimes erred; protecting his shortcomings he ultimately would not change; the emperor each time admonished him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as his tenure lengthened and business grew heavier, Vice Commissioners Zhao Changyan and Kou Zhun, both sharp-tongued, treated him with contempt; Xian sometimes blundered yet clung to his mistakes and would not amend them, and the emperor repeatedly admonished him to his face.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年八月，詔加切責，黜授隨州刺史，充崇信軍節度、觀察等使，遣之任。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Chunhua, an edict added stern rebuke; demoted and appointed prefect of Sui; filled the posts of Chongxin Army military commissioner and observation commissioner; sent to his assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Chunhua sharp rebuke was issued; he was demoted to prefect of Sui, made military and observation commissioner of Chongxin Army, and sent to his post.

sentences.zh: 俄知永興軍，徙延州。

translations.literal: Soon he knew Yongxing Army; transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed the Yongxing Military Commission, then was transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時夏臺、益部寇擾，顯上疏曰：「間歲以來，戎事未息，李繼遷負恩於靈、夏，王小波干紀於巴、邛，河右坤維並興師旅。

translations.literal: At the time Xia Terrace and Yibu were disturbed by raids; Xian memorialized: "In recent years military affairs have not ceased; Li Jiqian has been ungrateful in Ling and Xia; Wang Xiaobo has violated discipline in Ba and Qiong; Hexi and Kunwei have both raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: While Xia and Yibu were troubled by raids, Xian memorialized, "In recent years the frontier has not been quiet: Li Jiqian has turned ungrateful in Ling and Xia, Wang Xiaobo has rebelled in Ba and Qiong, and armies have been raised both in Hexi and in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 而繼遷翻然向化，遣子入覲，願修職貢。

translations.literal: Yet Jiqian suddenly turned toward civilization, sent his son to audience, and wished to restore tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jiqian has suddenly turned toward submission, sent his son to court, and asked to resume tribute.

sentences.zh: 陛下曲加容納，許其內附，示以德信，伸以恩錫，所以綏懷之者至矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has bent to accommodate and accept, permitted his inner submission, displayed virtue and trust, extended favor and gifts—the means of soothing and cherishing him have reached their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has graciously accepted him, allowed his submission, shown virtue and trust, and extended favor and gifts—the measures taken to win him over could hardly go further.

sentences.zh: 然而狼子野心，未可深信。

translations.literal: However the wolf-cub's wild heart cannot be deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heart of a wolf cub cannot be trusted too far.

sentences.zh: 所宜謹屯戍，固城壘，積芻糧，然後遴選才勇，付以邊任，縱有緩急，則備禦有素，彼又奚能為患哉？

translations.literal: What is fitting is carefully to garrison, solidify walls and ramparts, stock fodder and grain, then select talent and courage and entrust border duties; even if there is urgency, defenses will be prepared by habit—how then could they again become a calamity?
translations.idiomatic: What is needed is to keep garrisons alert, strengthen walls and ramparts, stock fodder and grain, and then choose able and brave men for the frontier posts; then even in an emergency defenses will already be in order, and what harm can they do?

sentences.zh: 至若蜀寇未平，神人共憤，謂宜申飭將帥，速期蕩平，既免老師以費財，且防事久則生變。

translations.literal: As for the Shu bandits not yet pacified, gods and men share anger; it is said one should admonish generals and commanders and quickly set a term for sweeping pacification, both to avoid an aged army wasting wealth and to guard against long affairs giving birth to change.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Shu rebels, gods and men alike are indignant; the generals should be sharply admonished to set a quick term for their suppression, both to spare the treasury the cost of a long campaign and to guard against trouble bred by delay.

sentences.zh: 又況邛、蜀物產殷富，其間士卒驕怠，遲留顧戀，實兼有之。

translations.literal: Moreover Qiong and Shu are rich in products; among them soldiers grow proud and slack, linger and look back fondly—both are truly present.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qiong and Shu are rich in goods, and the troops there grow proud, slack, and reluctant to leave—both evils are real.

sentences.zh: 莫若勿憚往來，潛為更代，既可均其勞逸，抑可免於遷延。

translations.literal: Better not to fear coming and going, secretly to rotate replacements—this can both balance their labor and rest and also avoid delay.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better not to shrink from rotation, but quietly to relieve units in turn, balancing labor and rest while avoiding endless delay.

sentences.zh: 至於河北關防所當加謹者，誠以國家方事西南，密謀興舉，若分中朝之勢力，則長外寇之姦謀矣。」

translations.literal: As for the Hebei passes that should be treated with added caution, truly because the state is now engaged in the southwest and secretly plans undertakings, if central court strength is divided, then outer enemies' treacherous schemes will grow long."
translations.idiomatic: As for the Hebei passes, added caution is needed because the state is now engaged in the southwest and secretly planning operations there; to divide the court's strength would only encourage the enemy's designs."

sentences.zh: 時制沿邊糧斛不許過河西，河西青鹽不得過界販鬻，犯者不以多少，處斬。

translations.literal: At the time regulations along the border did not permit grain to cross west of the river; west-of-river green salt was not permitted to be sold across the border; violators regardless of amount were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations then forbade frontier grain from crossing west of the river and forbade the sale of western green salt across the border; violators were executed regardless of quantity.

sentences.zh: 顯請犯多者依法，自餘別為科斷，以差其罪。

translations.literal: Xian requested that heavy offenders be punished by law, while the rest be separately sentenced to grade their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked that the worst offenders be punished by law while the rest receive graded sentences according to the offense.

sentences.zh: 章上未報，移知秦州。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not answered; he was transferred to know Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered, and he was transferred to govern Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，溫仲舒知州日，開拓山林，諷藩部獻其地。

translations.literal: At first when Wen Zhongshu knew the prefecture, he opened mountains and forests and prompted frontier tribes to offer their lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhongshu had governed the prefecture, he had opened mountains and forests and prompted frontier tribes to offer their lands.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷雖嘗給還，而採伐如故。

translations.literal: Later the court though once had returned them, logging continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court had later returned some of the land, yet logging continued as before.
