sentences.zh: 轉運使盧知翰請量給蕃部茶綵，以酬所獻，詔遣張從式與顯同往規度。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Lu Zhihan requested measuring out tea and silks to frontier tribes to repay what was offered; an edict sent Zhang Congshi and Xian together to survey and plan.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Lu Zhihan asked that tea and silks be measured out to the tribes in compensation for their lands, and an edict sent Zhang Congshi and Xian together to survey the matter.

sentences.zh: 顯言：「乃者朝命以趙保吉修貢，邊城務使安靜，若今動眾開斥疆境，非便。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "Recently the court ordered Zhao Baoji to maintain tribute; frontier cities must be kept quiet; if now we mobilize crowds to open and push the border, it is not advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The court has lately ordered Zhao Baoji to resume tribute and wants the frontier kept quiet; to mobilize men now and push the border outward would be unwise."

sentences.zh: 議遂罷。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，入朝，改橫海軍節度，出知鎮州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he entered court; changed to Henghai Army military commissioner; sent out to know Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he came to court, was made military commissioner of Henghai Army, and went out to govern Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，曹彬卒，復拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Cao Bin died; he was again appointed Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after Cao Bin died, he was again appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifice, added Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice he was given the additional title of Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸大名，內樞惟顯與副使宋湜從，言者多謂顯專司兵要，謀略非長。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited Daming, within the pivot only Xian and Vice Commissioner Song Shi followed; many speakers said Xian exclusively managed military essentials but was not strong in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong visited Daming, only Xian and Vice Commissioner Song Shi accompanied him within the Military Affairs Bureau, and many said that while Xian handled military essentials well, strategy was not his strength.

sentences.zh: 會湜卒，乃以參知政事向敏中權同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Shi died, Participating in Governance Xiang Minzhong was made acting jointly knowing Military Affairs Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, Vice Grand Councilor Xiang Minzhong was made acting co-head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年春，改授山南東道節度、同中書門下平章事、定州路行營都部署、河北都轉運使兼知定州。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, changed and appointed military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Dingzhou Route campaign deployment commissioner, Hebei chief transport commissioner while also knowing Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was reassigned as military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, made a Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, campaign deployment commissioner of the Dingzhou Route, chief transport commissioner of Hebei, and prefect of Ding.

sentences.zh: 秋，吏民詣駐泊都部署孔守正言顯治狀，願借留。

translations.literal: In autumn, officials and people went to garrison deployment commissioner Kong Shouzheng to speak of Xian's governance and wished to borrow and retain him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the officials and people appealed to garrison deployment commissioner Kong Shouzheng, praising Xian's administration and asking that he be kept longer.

sentences.zh: 守正以聞。

translations.literal: Shouzheng reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，加鎮、定、高陽關三路都部署，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: The next autumn, added deployment commissioner of the three routes Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass; permitted discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was also made deployment commissioner of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass routes and allowed to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 十月，契丹入寇，前軍過威虜軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Khitan invaded; the vanguard passed Weilu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Khitan invaded, and their vanguard passed Weilu Army.

sentences.zh: 比時方積雨，契丹以皮為弦，濕緩不堪用，顯因大破之，梟獲名王、貴將十五人及羽林印二鈕，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: At that time rain had just accumulated; the Khitan used leather for bowstrings, which when wet were slack and unusable; Xian therefore routed them greatly, displayed and captured fifteen named kings and noble generals and two Imperial Guard seal knobs, and beheaded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had been falling steadily, and the Khitan bowstrings of leather had gone slack and useless in the wet; Xian therefore inflicted a great defeat, captured fifteen named princes and noble generals along with two Imperial Guard seal knobs, and took twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 顯上言：「先奉詔令於近邊布陣，及應援北平控扼之路。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized: "Earlier I received an edict ordering deployment near the border and to support and control the routes to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Xian memorialized, "I had earlier been ordered to deploy near the border and to cover the routes supporting Beiping.

sentences.zh: 無何，敵騎已越亭障，顯之前陣雖有捷克，終違詔命。」

translations.literal: Before long the enemy cavalry had already crossed the pavilions and barriers; though Xian's forward array had merit in victory, in the end it violated the edict command."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy cavalry had crossed our outposts; though my forward line won a victory, I still disobeyed the edict in the end."

sentences.zh: 上章請罪。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 上降手劄，以慰其憂悸。

translations.literal: The emperor sent down a handwritten note to comfort his worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a handwritten note to comfort his anxiety.

sentences.zh: 明年，求致仕，不許，改河陽三城節度。

translations.literal: The next year he requested retirement; it was not permitted; changed to military commissioner of Heyang Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he asked to retire, but was refused and made military commissioner of Heyang Three Cities instead.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，時議親征契丹，顯言：「盛寒在序，敵未犯塞，鑾輿輕舉，直抵窮邊，寇若不逢，師乃先老。

translations.literal: About to go to his command, at the time discussion favored the emperor personally campaigning against the Khitan; Xian said: "Deep cold is in sequence; the enemy has not yet violated the border; the imperial carriage lightly undertakes the journey straight to the remote frontier—if the bandits are not met, the army will age first.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to take up his post, the court was debating an imperial campaign against the Khitan; Xian said, "Deep winter is upon us and the enemy has not yet crossed the border; if the imperial carriage moves lightly all the way to the remote frontier and the foe is not met, the army will wear itself out first.

sentences.zh: 況今繼遷未滅，西鄙不寧，儻北邊部落，與之結援，則中國之患，未可量也。

translations.literal: Moreover now Jiqian is not destroyed and the western border is not tranquil; if northern border tribes join aid with him, then China's calamity cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jiqian is not yet destroyed and the western frontier is unsettled; if northern tribes were to ally with him, the harm to the empire could hardly be measured.

sentences.zh: 議者乃於此時請復幽薊，非計之得也。

translations.literal: Those debating now at this time request recovering You and Ji—it is not a plan that succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: For advocates now to urge recovering You and Ji is no winning plan.

sentences.zh: 凡建議大事，上下協力，舉必成功。

translations.literal: Whenever proposing great affairs, above and below cooperate in strength; the undertaking will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great affairs are proposed, success depends on cooperation above and below.

sentences.zh: 今公卿士大夫以至庶人，尚有異同，未可謂為萬全之舉。

translations.literal: Now from grandees and scholar-officials down to commoners there are still differences; it cannot be called a ten-thousandfold safe undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: From grandees and scholar-officials down to commoners there are still disagreements, so this cannot be called a perfectly safe course.

sentences.zh: 若能選擇將帥，訓練士卒，堅城壘而繕甲兵，亦足以待敵矣。

translations.literal: If one can select generals and commanders, train soldiers, solidify walls and ramparts and repair armor and weapons, that is also sufficient to await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If generals are chosen well, troops trained, walls strengthened, and arms repaired, that is enough to await the enemy.

sentences.zh: 必欲復燕、薊舊地，則必修文德、養勇銳，同時之利，以奉行天罰而後可。」

translations.literal: If one must recover the old lands of Yan and Ji, then one must cultivate civil virtue, nurture courage and sharpness, seize the advantage of the moment, and only then carry out Heaven's punishment."
translations.idiomatic: If Yan and Ji must be recovered, civil virtue must be cultivated and bold troops nurtured so that when the moment is ripe Heaven's punishment may be carried out."

sentences.zh: 景德初，徙知天雄軍府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, transferred to know Tianxiong Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he was transferred to head the Tianxiong Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 又言：「祖宗以來，多命近臣統領軍旅。

translations.literal: He also said: "From the ancestors onward, many orders were given to close ministers to command armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Since the founding ancestors, close ministers have often been put in command of armies.

sentences.zh: 今後宣徽使，宜於文武群臣中擇曉達邊事者為之。

translations.literal: Hereafter Palace Directorate commissioners should be chosen from civil and military ministers who understand border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Palace Directorate commissioners should be chosen from among civil and military ministers who understand frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 蓋位高則威名著，識遠則勳勞立故也。

translations.literal: For when rank is high then prestige and name are established; when knowledge is far-reaching then merit and labor are set up.
translations.idiomatic: High rank brings renown, and far-sighted knowledge establishes merit—that is why.

sentences.zh: 武臣以罪黜者，宜加容貸，不以一眚遂廢，苟用之有恩，必得其死力，故曰『使功不如使過』也。

translations.literal: Military officials dismissed for crimes should receive added tolerance and pardon, not be discarded for one fault; if employed with grace, they will surely give their utmost strength unto death; therefore it is said 'employing merit is not as good as employing fault.'
translations.idiomatic: Military officials dismissed for offenses should be shown forbearance and not cast aside for a single fault; if used with kindness they will give their utmost, as the saying goes, 'It is better to employ a man for his fault than for his merit.

sentences.zh: 至若臨敵命將，則貴專任，出師應敵，則約束將校，使相應援。

translations.literal: As for appointing generals facing the enemy, what is prized is sole responsibility; when armies go out to meet the enemy, generals and officers are bound so they mutually support.
translations.idiomatic: When appointing generals on the eve of battle, sole responsibility is prized; when armies march out, officers should be bound to one another so they can support each other.

sentences.zh: 全是數者，則軍威倍壯，人心增勇矣。」

translations.literal: When numbers are complete, then military prestige is doubled in strength and men's hearts grow braver."
translations.idiomatic: When forces are complete in number, military prestige doubles and men's hearts grow bolder."

sentences.zh: 既而上表請赴行在，從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting to go to the mobile court; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized asking to join the mobile court, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: That autumn he was sent back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，上議親征。

translations.literal: The Khitan invaded; the emperor debated a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, the emperor debated leading the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 顯復陳三策，謂：「大軍方在鎮、定，契丹必不南侵，車駕止駐澶淵，詔鎮、定出兵，會河南軍，合擊之可也。

translations.literal: Xian again presented three strategies, saying: "The great army is just at Zhen and Ding; the Khitan surely will not invade south; the imperial carriage need only halt at Chanyuan; order Zhen and Ding to send troops, join Henan armies, and strike together—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: Xian again offered three plans, saying, "The main army is at Zhen and Ding, so the Khitan will surely not push south; let the imperial carriage halt at Chanyuan, order Zhen and Ding to march out, join the Henan forces, and strike together—that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 若契丹母子虛張聲勢，以抗我師，潛遣銳兵南攻駕前諸軍，則令鎮、定之師直衝戎帳，攻其營砦，則沿河遊兵不戰而自屈矣。

translations.literal: If the Khitan mother and son falsely display momentum to resist our army while secretly sending sharp troops south to attack the armies before the carriage, then order the Zhen and Ding armies straight to rush the barbarian headquarters and attack their camps and stockades—the roaming troops along the river will submit without battle.
translations.idiomatic: If the Khitan queen and heir merely feign strength to hold our army while secretly sending elite troops south against the forces before the carriage, let the Zhen and Ding armies strike straight at the barbarian headquarters and storm their camps; the river patrols will then collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 否則遣騎兵千、步兵三千於濮州渡河，橫掠澶州，繼以大軍追北掩擊，亦可出其不意也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise send one thousand cavalry and three thousand infantry to cross the river at Pu Prefecture, sweep across Cao Prefecture, then follow with the great army pursuing north in concealed strike—this too can catch them unawares."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise send one thousand cavalry and three thousand infantry to cross at Pu Prefecture, raid across Cao Prefecture, and follow with the main army in a concealed pursuit from the north—that too would catch them unawares."

sentences.zh: 已而契丹請盟，趙德明遣使修貢稱藩，朝廷加賞錫，且許通青鹽以濟邊民，從顯之請也。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan requested alliance; Zhao Deming sent envoys to restore tribute and declare vassalage; the court added rewards and gifts, and moreover permitted green salt to pass to aid border people—following Xian's request.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan sought peace, Zhao Deming sent envoys with tribute and declared himself a vassal, and the court added rewards and also allowed green salt to be traded to aid the frontier people, following Xian's request.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，被病，詔中使偕尚醫療視。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year he fell ill; an edict ordered a palace envoy together with the imperial physician to treat and observe him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he fell ill, and an edict sent a palace envoy with the imperial physician to treat him.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，許還京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, permitted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he was permitted to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時車駕上陵，顯謂賓佐曰：「余年位偕極，今天子道出虎牢，不得一拜屬車之塵，是遺恨也！」

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was ascending the mausoleum; Xian told his guests and aides: "My remaining years and rank have reached the extreme; today the Son of Heaven's road passes through Hulao—I cannot once bow to the dust of the attendant carriage; this is a remaining regret!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then visiting the imperial tombs; Xian told his staff, "My years and rank have both reached their height, yet as the Son of Heaven passes through Hulao I cannot even once bow to the dust of his attendant carriage—that will be my lasting regret!"

sentences.zh: 言訖涕下，至京，信宿卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: When the words ended tears fell; reaching the capital, within two nights he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, tears fell; he reached the capital and died within two nights at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 車駕至鄭州，聞之，遣宮苑使鄧永遷馳還護喪，贈中書令，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Zheng Prefecture and heard it, Palace Garden Commissioner Deng Yongqian was sent racing back to guard the funeral; posthumously made Secretariat Director; posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Zheng Prefecture and heard the news, he sent Palace Garden Commissioner Deng Yongqian racing back to oversee the funeral, posthumously made Xian Secretariat Director, and gave him the title Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: 錄其二子。

translations.literal: His two sons were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 顯自三班不數年正樞任，獎擢之速，時無擬之者。

translations.literal: Xian from the Three Classes within not many years reached the regular Military Affairs post; the speed of reward and promotion had no parallel in his time.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Classes Xian reached the headship of the Bureau of Military Affairs within only a few years, a pace of promotion unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 顯吏軍司時，張永德以滑州節制為殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: When Xian was a clerk in the army office, Zhang Yongde with Huazhou military control was Hall Front Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was still a clerk in the army office, Zhang Yongde, then military commissioner of Huazhou, was Chief Inspector of the Hall Front Office.

sentences.zh: 及顯自樞密鎮孟津兼相帥，永德由太子太師為相帥，同日宣制，永德兼大夫反在顯下，時人訝之。

translations.literal: When Xian from Military Affairs commanded Mengjin while also chancellor-commander, Yongde from Crown Prince Grand Mentor became chancellor-commander; on the same day the appointment was proclaimed; Yongde's concurrent grandee rank was instead below Xian's; people of the time were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian left the Bureau of Military Affairs to command Mengjin while also serving as chancellor-commander, Yongde moved from Crown Prince Grand Mentor to the same dual role; their appointments were proclaimed the same day, yet Yongde's concurrent grandee rank still stood below Xian's, to the astonishment of the day.

sentences.zh: 顯居中執政，矯情以厚胥吏，齪齪自固而已。

translations.literal: Xian holding the center in governance put on feeling to enrich clerks; he was petty and self-protective only.
translations.idiomatic: At the center of government Xian affected sentiment to enrich his clerks and was merely petty and self-protective.

sentences.zh: 在藩鎮，頗縱部曲擾下，論者非之。

translations.literal: In frontier commands he quite allowed subordinates to disturb those below; commentators criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: In frontier commands he allowed his subordinates to harass the people, and critics condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 子希逸，字仲莊，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Son Xiyi, styled Zhongzhuang, by yin privilege appointed Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiyi, whose style name was Zhongzhuang, entered service by yin privilege as an Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 好學，尤熟唐史，聚書萬餘卷。

translations.literal: He loved learning, especially knew Tang history well, and gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, was especially versed in Tang history, and collected more than ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 換秩授朝奉大夫、太子中允。

translations.literal: Exchanging rank he was appointed Court Gentleman for Court Audience and Crown Prince Middle Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged rank for the posts of Court Gentleman for Court Audience and Crown Prince Middle Attendant.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，改殿中丞、直史館，預修《冊府元龜》，加祠部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, changed to Palace Directorate Assistant, Direct Historiographer, participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Archive, added Ministry of Rites junior officer, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he became Palace Directorate Assistant and Direct Historiographer, took part in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Archive, was made a junior officer in the Ministry of Rites, and died.

sentences.zh: 希範至如京副使。

translations.literal: Xifan reached Deputy Envoy to the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan rose to Deputy Envoy to the Capital.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自柴禹錫而下，率因給事藩邸，以攀附致通顯者凡七人。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From Chai Yuxi downward, all because they attended the prince's establishment and through attachment achieved prominent passage were seven men in total.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: From Chai Yuxi downward, seven men in all won prominence by attending the princely establishment and attaching themselves to the future emperor.

sentences.zh: 若守一之質直，趙鎔之勤謹，服勞雖久而益修乃職，則其被眷遇也宜矣。

translations.literal: As for Shouyi's uprightness, Zhao Rong's diligence and care—though serving long they ever more cultivated their duties—then their receiving favor was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as the upright Shouyi and the diligent Zhao Rong, who though long in service only grew more careful in duty, deserved the favor they received.

sentences.zh: 張遜優於理財而未免於冒嫉，周瑩練習軍旅而頗傷於酷濫，禹錫素稱勤敏而不能不涉於朋比，王顯雖謹介自將而昧於學識，故莫逃於齪齪之譏。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun was superior in managing wealth but could not escape rash jealousy; Zhou Ying was practiced in armies but was quite harmed by cruelty and excess; Yuxi was always called diligent and alert yet could not avoid factional bonding; Wang Xian though careful and upright in self-conduct was dull in learning—thus none escaped the censure of pettiness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun excelled at finance yet could not escape charges of rash jealousy; Zhou Ying was skilled in military affairs yet marred by cruelty; Yuxi was famed for diligence yet could not avoid faction; Wang Xian was careful in conduct yet weak in learning—none escaped the charge of pettiness.

sentences.zh: 若以勤謹被信任，耆德冠樞宥，而善終如始者，其惟繼英乎。

translations.literal: If one considers being trusted through diligence and care, aged virtue crowning the Military Affairs precinct, and ending well as one began—perhaps only Jiying?
translations.idiomatic: But if one asks who was trusted for diligence, stood at the head of the Bureau of Military Affairs in honored age, and ended as he began, surely that was Jiying alone.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「君子有終，吉。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The noble man has an end—auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The noble man has a good end—auspicious."

sentences.zh: 此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant here.
